option_d: Presentations where the slide BACKGROUND STAYS FIXED while only the CONTENT (text; images) animates in — giving the impression of continuous flowing content

question: What is the CUBE transition?
option_a: The slide appears to ROTATE ON A 3D CUBE — the current slide rotates away and the next slide rotates into view on an adjacent face
option_b: The slide breaks into a checkerboard

question: What does the 'REVEAL' transition do in PowerPoint?
option_b: The current slide is WIPED AWAY like a curtain to REVEAL the next slide underneath
option_d: The slide rotates on a vertical axis

question: What is the GALLERY transition in PowerPoint?

option_d: A transition that shows all slides at once

question: In the Animation Pane; what does a GREEN bar represent?
option_d: An ENTRANCE animation — the object appears on the slide when this animation plays

question: In the Animation Pane; what does a RED bar represent?
option_a: EXIT animation — the object leaves the slide when this animation plays

question: What does 'BY 1ST LEVEL PARAGRAPHS' mean in Text Animation (Effect Options)?
option_a: The entire text box appears at once
option_b: Only the first bullet is animated

option_d: Each FIRST-LEVEL BULLET POINT (paragraph) is animated separately — so the presenter can reveal the text one bullet at a time

question: What does 'AS ONE OBJECT' mean in Text Animation (Effect Options)?
option_a: All text animates word by word

question: What does 'BY LETTER' animation sequence mean?
option_b: Each individual CHARACTER (letter) in the text flies in or fades in separately — creating a typewriter or showering effect

question: To CHANGE THE ORDER of animations in the Animation Pane; you?
option_a: Right-click and choose Move to Top

question: What is 'WIPE' as a PowerPoint transition?
option_c: The new slide is REVEALED gradually by a line sweeping across from one direction (e.g. left to right) — the old slide is wiped away as the new one appears

question: What is 'SPLIT' as a transition in PowerPoint?
option_a: The slide is divided into random shapes

question: What does the 'DRAPE' transition do in PowerPoint?
option_a: The slide appears to FOLD AND DRAPE like a curtain or fabric falling — a dramatic textured transition in the Exciting category
option_d: The slide tiles into smaller pieces

question: To add a SOUND to a specific ANIMATION (not a transition); you?
option_b: Animation → Effect Options → Effect tab → SOUND dropdown — choose a built-in sound or browse for a sound file

question: What does the 'GROW/SHRINK' emphasis animation do?
option_a: SCALES the object UP (grows) or DOWN (shrinks) by a percentage — drawing attention by temporarily enlarging or reducing it
option_b: Moves the object to a new position
option_d: Spins the object around its centre

question: What does the 'PULSE' emphasis animation do?
option_a: The object fades out then back
option_c: The object slides to a new position
option_d: The object RAPIDLY SCALES UP then back to original size — a quick pulsing beat that draws the eye

question: What does the 'TEETER' emphasis animation do?
option_c: Makes the object rotate back and forth LIKE A ROCKING OR TEETERING MOTION — a slight side-to-side rotation that draws attention

question: What is the 'BOUNCE' entrance animation?
option_a: The object fades in from top
option_c: The object FLIES IN from outside the slide and BOUNCES a few times before settling in its final position — as if it dropped and bounced like a ball

question: What is the 'ZOOM' entrance animation?
option_a: The object slides in from the left
option_b: The object GROWS from a tiny point to full size AT ITS POSITION on the slide — appearing to zoom toward the viewer

question: What is the 'FLY IN' entrance animation in PowerPoint?
option_a: The object FLIES IN FROM OUTSIDE THE SLIDE (default: from the bottom) and moves to its position on the slide

question: What does the 'FLOAT IN' entrance animation do?
option_a: Exactly the same as Fly In
option_c: The object appears with a bounce
option_d: The object APPEARS ABOVE ITS FINAL POSITION and FLOATS DOWN (or up) gently to settle in place — a softer; more graceful version of Fly In

question: What is the 'SWIVEL' entrance animation?
option_c: The object appears to SPIN ON A VERTICAL OR HORIZONTAL AXIS — rotating into view from an edge as if mounted on a hinge
option_d: The object grows from a point

question: In Book 5; students learn to use SOUND EFFECTS with transitions. What format does PowerPoint prefer for transition sounds?
option_a: WAV — the standard uncompressed audio format compatible with PowerPoint transition sound effects

question: A student has applied a 'FLY IN' animation to a title text and the text appears all at once. She wants each WORD to fly in separately. She should?
option_b: Change Effect Options → Sequence → 'BY WORD' — this makes each word in the text animate separately in sequence

question: What does the 'PATH POINTS' edit mode allow you to do for a Custom Motion Path?
option_d: RESHAPE the motion path by dragging its anchor points — add; delete; or move points to create curves and corners in the path

question: Which of the following animations would be BEST for making a company LOGO gradually appear on a title slide?
option_b: Appear Entrance (no movement; just instant reveal)
option_c: Fade Entrance — a professional; subtle appearance that draws attention without distraction

question: What does 'HIDE AFTER ANIMATION' (Effect Options → After animation) do?
option_b: The object moves off the slide

question: What is the purpose of NAMED OBJECTS in the Selection Pane for the Morph transition?
option_b: To give objects CONSISTENT NAMES across two consecutive slides so PowerPoint can match them and animate the differences smoothly using Morph

question: A student applies a theme and realises the BACKGROUND COLOUR is not ideal. Without changing the entire theme; she can?

option_c: Change the text colours in Home

question: What does 'REVERSE PATH DIRECTION' do for a Motion Path animation?
option_d: Makes the object travel the path in the OPPOSITE DIRECTION — start point becomes end point; end becomes start

question: What happens to an object set to 'HIDE ON NEXT MOUSE CLICK' after animation?
option_c: The object STAYS VISIBLE after its animation but DISAPPEARS when the presenter makes the next mouse click (or keypress)

question: In Book 5; students create a QUIZ slide using animations. What technique is taught for REVEALING ANSWERS one at a time?

option_c: Put all answers in a table

question: A student applies FIVE different transitions to FIVE slides. She later decides all slides should have the SAME FADE transition. What is the fastest method?

option_b: Delete all transitions and redo them

question: What view in PowerPoint is BEST for managing and reordering slides while checking which transitions are applied?
option_d: SLIDE SORTER VIEW (View → Slide Sorter) — shows all slide thumbnails with transition icons below each; and allows drag-and-drop reordering

question: In PowerPoint 2016; what does pressing F5 do during a presentation?
option_a: Starts the SLIDESHOW FROM THE FIRST SLIDE — the presentation goes full-screen from slide 1
option_d: Starts the slideshow from the current slide

question: What does pressing SHIFT+F5 do in PowerPoint?
option_c: Starts the slideshow FROM THE CURRENT SLIDE (not from slide 1) — useful for testing the current slide without going back to the beginning

question: What does ESCAPE (Esc) do when pressed during a PowerPoint slideshow?
option_b: Ends the slideshow and RETURNS TO NORMAL EDITING VIEW — the current slide stays selected

question: What does the 'HIDE SLIDE' feature do in PowerPoint?
option_a: MARKS A SLIDE so it is SKIPPED during the normal slideshow — the slide stays in the file but does not appear when pressing Next. It can be shown by typing its slide number during the show

question: What is the 'SCREEN RECORDING' feature in PowerPoint 2016 used for?
option_c: Recording the COMPUTER SCREEN and inserting the recording directly onto a slide as a video object

question: What is the difference between 'LOOP CONTINUOUSLY UNTIL ESC' and a fixed repeat count for an animation?
option_b: Loop Continuously keeps repeating the animation INDEFINITELY until Esc is pressed or until another trigger fires; a fixed count repeats it exactly N times then stops

question: What does 'SMOOTH START' and 'SMOOTH END' do in animation Effect Options Timing?
option_d: Causes the animation to START SLOWLY then speed up (Smooth Start) or SLOW DOWN before stopping (Smooth End) — creating a more natural; eased movement

question: In Book 5; students apply a theme to a presentation. After applying the theme; the teacher tells them to check that ALL TEXT IS STILL READABLE. Why might text become HARD TO READ after applying a theme?
option_a: A theme changes the slide BACKGROUND COLOUR — if existing text is dark on a white background; a theme with a dark background makes dark text invisible against dark

question: What is the ANIMATION PAINTER keyboard shortcut in PowerPoint?
option_d: There is no keyboard shortcut — only the toolbar button (double-click for multiple applications)

question: A student wants a PHOTO to stay HIDDEN; then APPEAR only when she clicks during her presentation. Which animation should she apply to the photo?
option_b: ENTRANCE → APPEAR (or Fade) with Start: On Click — the photo is invisible initially and appears when clicked

question: What does 'REWIND WHEN DONE PLAYING' do for an animation?

question: In Book 5 Chapter 4; what is the RECOMMENDATION about how many animations to use per slide for a professional presentation?
option_a: Use at MOST 2–3 animations per slide; focusing on animations that serve a purpose (revealing content gradually; emphasising key points) rather than decorating with effects for their own sake

question: What is the 'ORIGAMI' transition in PowerPoint 2016?
option_b: An Exciting category transition that makes the slide appear to FOLD like origami paper into a new shape revealing the next slide

question: What is a CUSTOM SLIDE SHOW in PowerPoint (Slide Show → Custom Slide Show)?
option_c: A SAVED SUBSET of slides from the full presentation that can be run independently — useful for presenting different versions to different audiences without maintaining separate files
option_d: A slideshow with custom animations only

question: What is the PHOTO ALBUM feature in PowerPoint 2016?
option_a: A feature to create slideshows of internet images
option_b: A feature to add a photo to a slide background
option_c: A feature to organise files in a folder
option_d: A built-in tool (Insert → Photo Album → New Photo Album) that automatically creates a new presentation with one or more photos per slide — imported from folders on the computer

question: To INSERT A PHOTO ALBUM in PowerPoint 2016; you go to?
option_b: Insert → Photo Album → New Photo Album

question: In the Photo Album dialog; what PICTURE LAYOUT options are available?
option_a: Fit to slide; 1 picture; 2 pictures; 4 pictures; 1 picture with title; 2 pictures with title; 4 pictures with title

question: What does the 'ALL PICTURES BLACK AND WHITE' checkbox do in the Photo Album dialog?
option_a: Prints the photos in black and white
option_c: Adds a black frame to each photo
option_d: Converts ALL IMPORTED PHOTOS to greyscale (black and white) in the presentation — a quick effect without editing each photo individually

question: What is the PURPOSE of the FRAME SHAPE option in the Photo Album dialog?
option_a: Adds a digital frame to the presentation background

option_d: Adds a text box around each photo

question: What does the 'CAPTIONS BELOW ALL PICTURES' option do in Photo Album?

question: To EDIT AN EXISTING Photo Album in PowerPoint?
option_b: Double-click a photo in the album

question: In the Photo Album dialog; the UP and DOWN ARROW buttons are used to?
option_d: REORDER the selected photo in the photo list — moving it higher or lower in the sequence of slides

question: Which BRIGHTNESS and CONTRAST tools appear in the Photo Album dialog?

question: What file types can be inserted as AUDIO in a PowerPoint 2016 presentation?

option_d: Only audio bought from the Microsoft Store

question: To INSERT AUDIO (background music or narration) in PowerPoint 2016?
option_a: Insert → Audio → AUDIO ON MY PC (browse for a local file) or RECORD AUDIO (record directly with a microphone)

question: After inserting audio; the AUDIO TOOLS tabs appear. What are they called?
option_b: FORMAT and PLAYBACK — Format handles the audio icon appearance; Playback handles how/when audio plays

question: What does the 'HIDE DURING SHOW' option do for an audio file?
option_b: Hides the audio WAVEFORM display on the slide

question: What does 'PLAY ACROSS SLIDES' mean for an audio file in PowerPoint?
option_a: The audio plays on one slide only

option_c: The audio CONTINUES PLAYING as the presentation advances through MULTIPLE slides without stopping — useful for background music throughout the presentation
option_d: The audio loops on the current slide

question: What does 'LOOP UNTIL STOPPED' do for audio in PowerPoint?
option_b: Makes the audio FILE REPEAT CONTINUOUSLY from the beginning when it ends — so background music keeps playing as long as the slide (or presentation) is shown

question: To TRIM AN AUDIO FILE in PowerPoint (removing the start or end)?
option_a: Audio Tools Playback → TRIM AUDIO — opens a dialog with a waveform and sliders to set a new start time and end time for the clip (the original file is unchanged)

question: What does the START dropdown (On Click or Automatically) control for audio in PowerPoint?
option_d: When the audio BEGINS PLAYING — 'On Click' waits for a mouse click; 'Automatically' plays the audio as soon as the slide appears

question: What file types can be inserted as VIDEO in PowerPoint 2016?
option_b: MP4; WMV; AVI; MOV; MPG; SWF (Flash; limited) and other common video formats

question: To INSERT A VIDEO FILE from your computer in PowerPoint 2016?
option_d: Insert → Video → VIDEO ON MY PC — browse for the video file to embed it into the slide

question: After inserting a video; what TWO contextual tabs appear in the ribbon?
option_b: Video Tools FORMAT and VIDEO TOOLS PLAYBACK — Format controls the video frame appearance; Playback controls how and when the video plays

question: What does 'PLAY FULL SCREEN' do for a video in PowerPoint?
option_a: During the slideshow; the video EXPANDS TO FILL THE ENTIRE SCREEN when played — then returns to the slide after playback

question: What does 'REWIND AFTER PLAYING' do for a video in PowerPoint?
option_d: After the video finishes playing; it AUTOMATICALLY RETURNS TO THE FIRST FRAME (the poster/thumbnail frame) — so the slide looks neat if reviewed again

question: To set a POSTER FRAME (a thumbnail image shown for the video before it plays) in PowerPoint?

question: To TRIM A VIDEO in PowerPoint (play only a portion of it)?

question: What does 'BOOKMARK' do for a video or audio file in PowerPoint?
option_a: Adds a TIME MARKER at a specific point in the playback timeline — can be used to trigger animations when the video reaches that point

question: What does SLIDE SHOW → SET UP SLIDE SHOW control?
option_d: Advanced SLIDE SHOW options: show type (Presented by speaker; Browsed by individual; Browsed at kiosk); show options (loop; narration; animations); which slides to show; and advance slides (manually or using timings)

question: What does the 'BROWSED AT A KIOSK' show type do in Set Up Slide Show?
option_a: Runs the slideshow in a small window

option_d: Plays the slideshow in a browser

question: What is the 'REHEARSE TIMINGS' feature in PowerPoint?

question: After REHEARSING TIMINGS; where can you see the recorded time for each slide?
option_a: Under each slide thumbnail in SLIDE SORTER view (the time appears below the slide thumbnail next to the transition star)

question: What is the purpose of 'RECORD SLIDE SHOW' in PowerPoint 2016?
option_a: Records NARRATION (voice-over using the microphone) and TIMINGS simultaneously as you present — syncing the audio narration to each slide for automated playback
option_c: Records the video from a camera

question: What is the file extension for a POWERPOINT SHOW file (a file that opens directly in Slideshow mode)?

question: To save a presentation as a POWERPOINT SHOW (.ppsx) file?

question: What is the PRESENTER VIEW in PowerPoint (Slide Show → Presenter View)?
option_c: A view that shows all slides simultaneously

question: What does the 'USE TIMINGS' checkbox in Set Up Slide Show control?
option_a: Whether the presentation uses the REHEARSED/RECORDED SLIDE TIMINGS for automatic advancement — unchecking it requires manual clicks even if timings were saved

question: What does the 'LOOP CONTINUOUSLY UNTIL ESC' checkbox do in Set Up Slide Show?

question: What does the 'SHOW WITHOUT NARRATION' checkbox do in Set Up Slide Show?
option_b: MUTES recorded narration during this playback of the presentation — the narration audio is still saved but will not play during this show

question: What is an 'ONLINE PRESENTATION' in PowerPoint 2016?
option_c: Embedding the file in a website

question: To ADD SPEAKER NOTES to a slide in PowerPoint?

question: What does PRINT → NOTES PAGES print in PowerPoint?

question: What does 'HANDOUTS' print in PowerPoint?
option_c: Multiple slides per page (1; 2; 3; 4; 6; or 9 slides per page) as small THUMBNAILS — for giving audience members a paper reference
option_d: Only the title of each slide

question: What is OUTLINE VIEW in PowerPoint?
option_a: A view that shows slide thumbnails only
option_b: A view that shows ALL TEXT from all slides in an OUTLINE FORMAT (by heading and bullets) with no images — useful for quickly editing text content across all slides

question: What is the purpose of the LASER POINTER during a slideshow in PowerPoint?

question: What does the PEN tool do during a slideshow in PowerPoint?

question: To INSERT ONLINE VIDEO (from YouTube) into a PowerPoint slide?

question: What does 'EMBED VIDEO' mean vs 'LINK TO VIDEO' in PowerPoint?

question: What is the 'COMPRESS MEDIA' feature in PowerPoint (File → Info → Compress Media)?
option_b: Reduces the FILE SIZE of embedded audio and video files by re-encoding them at a lower quality — options: Presentation Quality; Internet Quality; Low Quality

question: What does the EXPORT TO VIDEO feature do in PowerPoint 2016?
option_a: Embeds a video on a slide

question: What RESOLUTION options are available when exporting a presentation as video in PowerPoint?
option_c: Ultra HD (4K); Full HD (1080p); HD (720p); and Standard (480p)
option_d: Only the screen resolution of the computer

question: After exporting to VIDEO; an audience member can watch the PowerPoint presentation?

question: What is the purpose of the 'SECTIONS' feature in PowerPoint?

question: In Book 5 Chapter 5; what TYPE OF PRESENTATION do students build using Photo Album; audio; and slideshow features?
option_a: A PHOTO ESSAY or DIGITAL STORY — combining imported photos; background music; and automatic slide timings to create a self-running multimedia presentation

question: What does the 'SLIDE SHOW' tab → 'HIDE SLIDE' do to a presentation?

question: To navigate DIRECTLY TO A SPECIFIC SLIDE during a running slideshow?
option_d: TYPE THE SLIDE NUMBER then press ENTER — the presentation jumps directly to that slide number

question: What is the 'BLACK SCREEN' shortcut during a PowerPoint slideshow?
option_c: B or . (full stop) — pressing B or period makes the screen go BLACK; hiding the current slide from the audience (press again to return to the slide)

question: In Book 5; students learn to save a presentation as PDF. What is the advantage of PDF over PPSX?
option_d: A PDF DOES NOT REQUIRE POWERPOINT to open — it shows slides as fixed images in any PDF viewer; on any device; with no animation or interactivity but guaranteed visual fidelity

question: What is a CUSTOM SLIDE SHOW in PowerPoint?
option_a: A SUBSET of slides from a presentation that you can name and run independently — (Slide Show → Custom Slide Show → Custom Shows → New) — useful for tailoring presentations for different audiences without duplicating the file
option_c: A show with a custom background

question: What keyboard shortcut STARTS a PowerPoint slideshow from SLIDE 1?
option_b: F5 — starts from the very first slide regardless of which slide is currently selected

question: What keyboard shortcut STARTS a PowerPoint slideshow from the CURRENT SLIDE?
option_c: Shift+F5 — starts the slideshow from whichever slide is selected in Normal view

question: To ADD AUDIO that plays AUTOMATICALLY when a specific slide appears?
option_d: Insert → Audio → Audio on My PC → after inserting; set Audio Tools Playback → Start → Automatically

question: What is the AUDIO ICON that appears on a slide after inserting audio?
option_b: A SPEAKER ICON (loudspeaker symbol) — the default visual marker for an embedded or linked audio clip on a slide

question: To make background music FADE IN at the beginning of an audio clip in PowerPoint?
option_a: Audio Tools Playback → FADE IN (set a duration in seconds) — the audio will gradually increase from silence to full volume over the specified time

question: To make background music FADE OUT at the end of an audio clip?
option_d: Audio Tools Playback → FADE OUT (set a duration in seconds) — the audio gradually decreases to silence at the end of the clip

question: What is the VOLUME control for audio in PowerPoint's Playback tab?
option_b: A dropdown with four settings: Low; Medium; High; and Mute — sets the default playback volume for the clip

question: What file format does PowerPoint EXPORT to when creating a video using 'Create a Video' (File → Export)?

question: When inserting a VIDEO from a local file; what does PowerPoint do with the video file by DEFAULT?

question: What SECTION of the RIBBON appears when you click on an embedded VIDEO object on a slide?
option_d: Video Tools — with FORMAT and PLAYBACK tabs that are specific to video objects

question: What does 'HIDE WHILE NOT PLAYING' do for a video in PowerPoint?

option_c: Hides the video from the slide panel

question: What does the DURATION field in the TRANSITIONS tab control?

option_d: The time before the transition starts

question: What is the MORPH TRANSITION in PowerPoint 2016?

question: For MORPH transition to work correctly with text or images; what must be TRUE about objects on consecutive slides?

question: What is SLIDE SORTER VIEW in PowerPoint (View → Slide Sorter)?

question: What keyboard shortcut DUPLICATES a slide in PowerPoint?

question: What does 'APPLY TO ALL' in the Transitions tab do?

option_c: Applies the layout to all slides
option_d: Applies the SELECTED TRANSITION (including its settings: effect options; duration; sound; advance timing) to EVERY SLIDE in the presentation — a one-click way to set a consistent transition throughout

question: What is the READING VIEW in PowerPoint?
option_a: A simplified SLIDESHOW VIEW within the PowerPoint window (not full-screen) — useful for reviewing the presentation with all animations and transitions playing; without switching to full-screen mode
option_c: A view that shows only text

question: What does FILE → INFO → CHECK COMPATIBILITY do in PowerPoint 2016?
option_b: Checks if the file is corrupted
option_d: Checks whether the presentation uses features that are NOT supported by OLDER versions of PowerPoint (2003; 2007; 2010) — and lists any potential issues

question: What does 'INSPECT DOCUMENT' (File → Info → Check for Issues → Inspect Document) do?
option_b: Searches for HIDDEN DATA in the presentation — such as speaker notes; comments; hidden slides; author metadata; personal information; and invisible objects — so you can remove them before sharing

question: What PRINT LAYOUT prints slides with LINES for audience notes in PowerPoint?

question: What is the DEFAULT FILE FORMAT for saving a PowerPoint 2016 presentation?

question: In the Photo Album dialog; what is 'FIT TO SLIDE' layout?

question: What type of audio file is BEST for background music in a PowerPoint presentation?
option_c: MP3 — a good balance of quality and FILE SIZE; widely supported by PowerPoint; small enough not to inflate the presentation file excessively

question: To INSERT AUDIO FROM A MICROPHONE directly in PowerPoint without a separate app?
option_b: Insert → Audio → Record Audio — opens a recording dialog where you click the red dot to start recording; then the square to stop; then name the clip and click OK to insert

question: After recording audio with 'Record Audio' in PowerPoint; where does the audio appear?
option_b: As a SPEAKER ICON on the slide — the same as any other embedded audio; with the same Audio Tools FORMAT and PLAYBACK tabs available

question: To REORDER photos in a Photo Album AFTER the album has been created?
option_a: Insert → Photo Album → Edit Photo Album → select a photo in the list → use the Up/Down ARROW buttons to move it; then click Update
option_d: Drag slides in Slide Sorter view

question: What does SLIDE SHOW → PLAY NARRATIONS checkbox control?
option_d: Whether PREVIOUSLY RECORDED NARRATIONS play during the slideshow — unchecking it silences narrations so a live presenter can speak without the recording playing over them

question: In Book 5; students learn to insert a VIDEO from their computer. What FORMAT is recommended for reliable playback in PowerPoint 2016?
option_c: .MP4 (H.264 video codec with AAC audio) — the most universally compatible video format for PowerPoint 2016 on Windows

question: What happens when you DOUBLE-CLICK a .ppsx file in Windows?

option_c: Opens in PowerPoint as a normal .pptx
option_d: Asks the user whether to edit or show

question: What does the SCREEN RECORDING feature do in PowerPoint 2016 (Insert → Screen Recording)?

option_d: Records the entire presentation as a video

question: What does clicking 'SAVE AS' (.ppsx) do differently from normal 'SAVE' (.pptx) in PowerPoint?
option_d: Creates a FILE THAT OPENS DIRECTLY IN SLIDESHOW MODE — saved as a PowerPoint Show (.ppsx) rather than an editable presentation (.pptx)

question: What SLIDE SHOW → MONITOR setting does when you have TWO DISPLAYS connected?
option_a: Lets you specify WHICH MONITOR shows the audience view (full-screen slides) and which shows Presenter View — ensuring the audience sees slides and the presenter sees notes + controls

question: What is the purpose of the TIMER DISPLAY in Presenter View during a slideshow?
option_b: Shows the countdown to the next slide

question: In Book 5's practical exercise; students create a multimedia presentation. What is the CORRECT ORDER of steps?

option_d: Insert Video → Insert Audio → Photo Album → Save as .pdf

question: What is a TRANSITION SOUND in PowerPoint (Transitions → Timing → Sound)?

question: What does 'ADVANCE SLIDE: AFTER' (a set time) do in the Transitions tab?
option_b: Shows the slide for that number of minutes
option_c: Fades the slide after the time
option_d: Automatically ADVANCES THE SLIDE to the next one after the specified time elapses — enabling self-running presentations without the need for manual clicks

question: What is the purpose of LINKING a video file in PowerPoint (rather than embedding it)?
option_c: Linking keeps the video file SEPARATE from the .pptx — the presentation stores only a pointer to the file; resulting in a SMALLER .pptx file; but the video file must always stay in the same relative location

question: What does the REMOVE BACKGROUND feature do in PowerPoint (available for images via Picture Tools → Format → Remove Background)?
option_b: Automatically removes the background from a PHOTO on a slide — keeping the main subject and making the rest transparent — using AI-based detection with pink highlights

question: When a SLIDE TRANSITION is set to 'ON MOUSE CLICK' and the presenter presses the SPACEBAR during a show; what happens?
option_a: The spacebar ADVANCES the slide — it acts like a mouse click; progressing to the next slide or the next animation on the current slide

question: What does pressing RIGHT ARROW key do during a PowerPoint slideshow?
option_d: Advances to the next slide or next animation — the same as a mouse click or spacebar press

question: What VIEW shows ALL SLIDES as equal-sized thumbnails and is most useful for REORDERING a long presentation?
option_c: SLIDE SORTER VIEW (View → Slide Sorter) — shows all slides as a grid; drag to reorder

question: What does the PAPER CLIP icon on a slide thumbnail in the slide panel indicate in PowerPoint?

question: In Book 5 Chapter 5; after the multimedia presentation is complete; students are asked to share it. What is the BEST way to share so the recipient does NOT need PowerPoint installed?
option_a: Export as VIDEO (.mp4) — plays in any video player on any device without PowerPoint; OR Export as PDF — opens in any PDF viewer

question: What is the INTERNET?
option_a: A single computer owned by a company
option_c: A wireless signal from a router
option_d: A GLOBAL NETWORK of millions of interconnected computers and devices that share information and resources using agreed-upon protocols (rules)

question: What is the WORLD WIDE WEB (WWW)?
option_b: A COLLECTION OF WEBSITES and web pages stored on web servers and accessed via the Internet using a web browser — it is only one part of the Internet
option_c: A type of cable used to connect computers

question: What is a WEB BROWSER?
option_d: A SOFTWARE APPLICATION (e.g. Microsoft Edge; Google Chrome; Mozilla Firefox; Safari) used to ACCESS and DISPLAY websites and web pages on the Internet

question: What is MICROSOFT EDGE?
option_c: Microsoft's built-in WEB BROWSER included with Windows 10 and 11 — it replaced Internet Explorer as Microsoft's default browser; built on the Chromium engine

question: What is a URL (Uniform Resource Locator)?
option_a: The UNIQUE WEB ADDRESS of a page or resource on the Internet — for example: https://www.bbc.com/news — that browsers use to locate and retrieve it

question: What does HTTP stand for?
option_b: HyperText Transfer Protocol — the rules for transmitting web pages between servers and browsers over the Internet

question: What does HTTPS mean and why is it important?
option_c: HyperText Transfer Protocol SECURE — an ENCRYPTED version of HTTP that protects data exchanged between your browser and the web server using SSL/TLS; shown as a padlock in the address bar

question: What is a SEARCH ENGINE?
option_a: A website that stores files for download
option_d: A WEB SERVICE (e.g. Google; Bing; Yahoo) that crawls the Internet to index web pages and then lets users find relevant pages by typing SEARCH QUERIES (keywords)

question: What is GOOGLE?
option_a: The world's most popular SEARCH ENGINE — accessed at www.google.com — that uses complex algorithms to rank billions of web pages by relevance to search queries

question: What is MICROSOFT BING?
option_c: Microsoft's SEARCH ENGINE (www.bing.com) — built into Windows and Microsoft Edge as the default search engine; with features like image search; video search; and news search

question: In the Microsoft Edge ADDRESS BAR; you can BOTH type a URL to go directly to a website AND type a search query. When you type a search term without a URL; Edge does what?
option_b: Sends the search query to the DEFAULT SEARCH ENGINE (Bing by default in Edge; or whichever is set) and shows results

question: What is the HOMEPAGE in a web browser?
option_a: The WEB PAGE that opens automatically when you launch the browser or click the Home button — set in browser Settings

question: What is a FAVOURITE / BOOKMARK in a web browser?
option_d: A SAVED SHORTCUT to a website or web page that lets you return to it quickly without retyping the URL — saved via the star icon in Edge or Ctrl+D

question: What does the BACK BUTTON (←) do in a web browser?
option_c: Goes BACK to the PREVIOUS web page in the current tab's history

question: What does the REFRESH / RELOAD button do in a web browser?
option_a: RE-LOADS the CURRENT web page — downloading a fresh copy from the server; updating any content that may have changed since the page was last loaded
option_b: Goes back to the previous page

question: What is a BROWSER TAB?
option_b: A SEPARATE BROWSING SESSION within the same browser window — each tab shows an independent web page; letting you open multiple websites simultaneously without opening multiple windows
option_c: A section of a web page

question: What keyboard shortcut opens a NEW TAB in most web browsers?
option_d: Ctrl+T — opens a new empty tab in the same browser window

question: What does CTRL+W do in a web browser?
What is PRIVATE BROWSING (InPrivate in Edge; Incognito in Chrome)?
option_a: Browsing that is invisible to the internet
option_d: A BROWSING MODE where the browser does NOT save the browsing history; cookies; form data; or passwords from that session — closed when the window is closed

question: To open an INCOGNITO window in Microsoft Edge (called InPrivate)?
option_b: Ctrl+Shift+N — opens a new InPrivate (private browsing) window where browsing history; cookies; and site data are not saved locally

question: What is an EMAIL ADDRESS? Give an example of its structure.
option_a: A unique IDENTIFIER for an email account in the format: username@domain.com — for example: student@school.edu — where @ separates the username from the domain

question: What is CYBERBULLYING?
option_d: Using digital technology (social media; messaging; gaming; email) to REPEATEDLY HARASS; THREATEN; HUMILIATE; or EMBARRASS another person — a form of bullying that occurs online or via devices

question: What should you do if you experience or witness CYBERBULLYING?
option_a: DO NOT respond to the bully; SAVE EVIDENCE (screenshots); BLOCK the bully; and TELL A TRUSTED ADULT (parent; teacher; school counsellor) immediately

question: What is a PHISHING ATTACK?
option_c: A FRAUDULENT ATTEMPT to steal personal information (passwords; credit card numbers; etc.) by disguising as a TRUSTWORTHY source — usually through fake emails; websites; or messages that look legitimate
option_d: A way to speed up internet connections

question: What is SPAM?
option_b: UNSOLICITED (unwanted) BULK EMAIL — usually commercial advertising; scams; or phishing attempts — sent to large numbers of recipients without their consent

question: What is MALWARE?
option_d: Malicious Software — programs designed to HARM; DISRUPT; or GAIN UNAUTHORISED ACCESS to a computer system — types include viruses; worms; Trojans; ransomware; and spyware

question: What is a COMPUTER VIRUS?
option_c: A TYPE OF MALWARE that ATTACHES ITSELF to legitimate files and REPLICATES — spreading to other files and computers when infected files are shared; it can damage data; slow the system; or cause other harm

question: What is ANTIVIRUS SOFTWARE?
option_a: Software that speeds up the internet
option_b: A SECURITY PROGRAM that detects; prevents; and removes malware (viruses; worms; Trojans; etc.) from a computer — examples include Windows Defender; Avast; Norton; and Kaspersky

question: What is a STRONG PASSWORD? Which of these is strongest?
option_a: P@55w0rd!#X9qR — long; uses uppercase; lowercase; numbers; and special characters; making it very hard to guess or crack

question: What is TWO-FACTOR AUTHENTICATION (2FA)?
option_a: A SECURITY METHOD that requires TWO forms of verification to log in — typically a PASSWORD (something you know) plus a SECOND FACTOR such as a code sent to your phone (something you have)

question: Why should you NEVER share personal information (full name; address; phone; school name) with strangers ONLINE?
option_a: Because it is against the law
option_b: Because the internet is always slow
option_c: Because strangers online may not be who they claim to be — sharing personal information with strangers online puts you at risk of identity theft; stalking; fraud; or other harms

question: What does CTRL+F do in a WEB BROWSER or document?
option_b: Finds (SEARCHES) for a word or phrase within the current web page or document — opens a search bar where you type the text and the browser highlights all matching instances on the page

question: To DOWNLOAD A FILE from the Internet in Edge or Chrome?
option_d: Right-click the file link → Save link as (or just click the link and the browser downloads it automatically) to save it to the chosen folder on the computer

question: What is an ISP (Internet Service Provider)?
option_a: A COMPANY that provides INTERNET ACCESS to homes; schools; and businesses — examples include local telecom companies; cable providers; and mobile operators

question: What is BANDWIDTH?
option_b: The AMOUNT OF DATA that can be transmitted over an internet connection per second — measured in Mbps (Megabits per second) or Gbps; higher bandwidth means faster internet
option_c: The number of web pages on the Internet
option_d: The strength of a Wi-Fi signal

question: What is WI-FI?
option_b: A type of cable for internet
option_c: WIRELESS networking technology that allows devices to connect to the Internet or a local network without physical cables — using radio signals from a WIRELESS ROUTER

question: What is a HOTSPOT?
option_c: A computer that has a virus
option_d: A location or device that provides a PUBLIC or SHARED Wi-Fi internet connection — such as a café; airport; school; or a mobile phone sharing its data connection

question: Why should you be CAREFUL using PUBLIC Wi-Fi hotspots?
option_a: Because public Wi-Fi is often UNENCRYPTED — anyone nearby can potentially intercept data you send and receive; so never log in to banking; email; or sensitive accounts on unsecured public Wi-Fi

question: What does COOKIES mean in the context of web browsing?
option_d: Small TEXT FILES stored on your computer by websites to REMEMBER information about you — such as login status; shopping cart contents; language preferences; and site settings

question: What is ONLINE SAFETY? Give TWO key rules.
option_c: Behaving responsibly and protecting yourself online — key rules include: (1) Never share personal information with strangers. (2) Tell a trusted adult if something makes you uncomfortable online.

question: What is NETIQUETTE?
option_b: ONLINE ETIQUETTE — the rules of polite; respectful; and responsible behaviour when communicating online (messaging; email; social media; forums)

question: What is a HYPERLINK?
option_b: A CLICKABLE LINK on a web page — usually formatted as underlined coloured text or an image — that navigates to another web page; document; or resource when clicked

question: What is CLOUD STORAGE?
option_b: A type of physical hard drive
option_d: Online storage services (e.g. OneDrive; Google Drive; iCloud) that store files on REMOTE SERVERS accessed via the Internet — letting you access files from any device anywhere

question: What is STREAMING?
option_c: Receiving and playing AUDIO or VIDEO in real time over the Internet WITHOUT DOWNLOADING the file first — examples: YouTube; Netflix; Spotify

question: What is SOCIAL MEDIA? Give an example.
option_a: Online PLATFORMS that let users CREATE and SHARE CONTENT and INTERACT with others — examples include Facebook; Instagram; TikTok; Twitter/X; Snapchat; YouTube

question: In Microsoft Edge; what is the READING VIEW?
option_a: A view to read computer manuals
option_b: A SIMPLIFIED VIEW that removes ads; navigation; and clutter from web pages to show just the ARTICLE TEXT and images — making it easier to read long articles
option_c: A view to read PDF files

question: What does DOWNLOADING mean?
option_a: Transferring a FILE from the INTERNET (a server) to YOUR COMPUTER — saving a local copy
option_b: Sending a file to the internet

question: What does UPLOADING mean?
option_d: Transferring files FROM YOUR COMPUTER to a server on the Internet — for example; sending a photo to social media; submitting work to a class website; or saving a file to cloud storage

question: Why is it important to EVALUATE THE RELIABILITY of websites found via search engines?
option_a: Because search engines rank paid sites first
option_b: Because all websites charge for access
option_c: Because anyone can publish ANYTHING on the Internet — not all information is accurate; up to date; or unbiased; some sites spread misinformation or are biased sources
option_d: Because websites are often in foreign languages

question: What does the PADLOCK ICON in the browser address bar mean?
option_a: The website is the official one
option_b: The website has been verified by Google
option_c: The connection to the website uses HTTPS — the communication between your browser and the server is ENCRYPTED; protecting data in transit from interception
option_d: The website is safe to download from

question: To SEARCH EFFECTIVELY with Google; what does putting a phrase in QUOTATION MARKS do?
option_b: Forces an EXACT PHRASE MATCH — only pages containing that EXACT phrase in that EXACT ORDER appear in results — useful for finding specific quotes; titles; or multi-word terms

question: What does using a MINUS SIGN in a Google search do (e.g. 'jaguars -cars')?
option_a: EXCLUDES pages containing the word after the minus sign — 'jaguars -cars' finds pages about Jaguar animals; excluding pages about Jaguar cars

question: To search ONLY within a specific WEBSITE using Google?
option_a: Click 'Search this site' on the page
option_c: Use the website's own search box only
option_d: Type 'site:website.com your search terms' in Google — e.g. 'site:bbc.com climate change' searches only the BBC website for 'climate change'

question: What is the DIFFERENCE between a SEARCH ENGINE and a WEB BROWSER?
option_c: A BROWSER is an application that displays web pages (Edge; Chrome; Firefox); a SEARCH ENGINE is a website/service that helps you FIND web pages (Google; Bing) — you use a browser to access a search engine
option_d: A browser can only open local files

question: What is a DOMAIN NAME in a URL? (e.g. 'google.com' in 'https://www.google.com/search')
option_a: The name of the web browser
option_b: The folder path after the first slash
option_d: The HUMAN-READABLE ADDRESS of a website (google.com; bbc.co.uk; etc.) that is translated by DNS into the numeric IP address of the server hosting the site

question: What does '.com' in a domain name indicate?
option_a: A COMMERCIAL organisation — '.com' is the most common top-level domain (TLD); originally for US commercial entities but now used worldwide by any organisation

question: What does '.edu' or '.ac.uk' in a domain name indicate?
option_b: An EDUCATIONAL or ACADEMIC institution — making it a reliable source for academic information

question: What is an IP ADDRESS?
option_c: A NUMERICAL LABEL (e.g. 192.168.1.1) assigned to every device on a network — the actual address computers use to find and communicate with each other on the Internet
option_d: A login name for a website

question: What is DNS (Domain Name System)?
option_d: The INTERNET'S 'PHONE BOOK' — a distributed system that translates HUMAN-READABLE domain names (google.com) into MACHINE-READABLE IP addresses so browsers can connect to the right servers

question: What is a WEB SERVER?
option_b: A COMPUTER that stores website files and sends them to browsers that request them — web servers run 24/7 and respond to HTTP/HTTPS requests from users worldwide

question: What does 'CACHE' mean in web browsing?
option_a: STORED COPIES of web pages; images; and files saved LOCALLY on your computer by the browser so that frequently visited pages load FASTER on repeat visits

question: What does CLEARING THE BROWSER CACHE do?
option_d: Removes LOCALLY STORED COPIES of web pages and media files — the browser must re-download fresh copies from the server; which can fix display problems but makes initial page loads slower

question: What is ONLINE PLAGIARISM?
option_a: Copying text; images; or ideas from the Internet and presenting them as YOUR OWN WORK without crediting the original source

question: What is COPYRIGHT? How does it apply to images found on the Internet?
option_a: Copyright means anything on the internet is free to use
option_c: Copyright gives the CREATOR of original work (text; images; music; video) EXCLUSIVE RIGHTS — images found on the Internet are usually protected by copyright and cannot be used without permission or a licence

question: What are CREATIVE COMMONS licences?
option_b: Licences that allow creators to grant PUBLIC PERMISSION to use their work under specific conditions — ranging from free to use for any purpose; to free for non-commercial use only; with or without credit required

question: What is GOOGLE CHROME?
option_d: Google's WEB BROWSER — a free browser developed by Google that is the most widely used browser globally; available for Windows; Mac; iOS; and Android

question: What is the DIFFERENCE between MICROSOFT EDGE and GOOGLE CHROME?
option_b: EDGE is made by MICROSOFT (pre-installed on Windows); CHROME is made by GOOGLE (must be downloaded separately) — both are Chromium-based browsers but are separate products with different features and defaults
option_c: Edge is faster than Chrome always
option_d: Chrome can only be used on Google devices

question: When using a SEARCH ENGINE; what are SPONSORED (AD) RESULTS?
option_c: PAID ADVERTISEMENTS that appear at the TOP of search results — marked as 'Sponsored' or 'Ad' — companies pay the search engine to appear at the top for specific search terms

question: What does 'SAFE SEARCH' do on a search engine?
option_a: FILTERS OUT explicit; adult; or inappropriate content from search results — most search engines offer SafeSearch settings to help filter unwanted content for younger users

question: In Google; how do you search for IMAGES only?
option_a: Click the 'Images' tab at the top of Google search results — this filters results to show only images rather than web pages

question: What is EMAIL (Electronic Mail)?
option_c: A DIGITAL MESSAGING SERVICE that allows text messages; attachments (files; images); and links to be sent between users over the Internet — almost instantly; to anyone in the world with an email address

question: What does CC mean in an email?
option_b: Carbon Copy — ADDITIONAL RECIPIENTS who receive a copy of the email; visible to all other recipients

question: What does BCC mean in an email?
option_d: Blind Carbon Copy — sends a copy to additional recipients whose email addresses are HIDDEN from all other recipients

question: What is an EMAIL ATTACHMENT?
option_a: A FILE (document; image; PDF; video; etc.) that is ATTACHED to an email message and sent along with it — the recipient can download and open the attached file
option_c: A photo in the email body

question: Why should you NEVER open email attachments from UNKNOWN senders?
option_a: Because the attachment might be large
option_d: Because attachments from unknown senders may contain MALWARE (viruses; Trojans; ransomware) that infect your computer when opened — a common method for spreading malicious software

question: What is RANSOMWARE?
option_b: A type of MALWARE that ENCRYPTS a victim's files and demands a RANSOM PAYMENT to restore access — victims cannot open their own files unless they pay or have backups

question: What is SPYWARE?
option_c: MALWARE that secretly MONITORS and COLLECTS information about a user's activities (keystrokes; passwords; browsing history; financial data) and sends it to a third party WITHOUT the user's knowledge

question: What is a FIREWALL?
option_a: A SECURITY SYSTEM (hardware or software) that MONITORS and CONTROLS incoming and outgoing network traffic based on security rules — blocking unauthorised access to or from a private network

question: What is a VPN (Virtual Private Network)?
option_d: A SERVICE that creates an ENCRYPTED TUNNEL for internet traffic; routing it through a server in another location — hiding the user's real IP address and protecting data from interception

question: What does the term 'GOING VIRAL' mean on the internet?
option_c: When a piece of online CONTENT (video; image; article; meme) SPREADS RAPIDLY across the internet — shared by millions of people in a short time — reaching a huge audience organically
option_d: When a file is uploaded to the internet

question: What is FAKE NEWS?
option_b: FALSE or MISLEADING INFORMATION presented as NEWS — deliberately created to deceive; influence opinion; or spread for entertainment; often shared on social media before being fact-checked

question: What is the purpose of a CAPTCHA on websites?
option_b: To verify that the USER is a HUMAN and not an automated bot — by presenting a challenge (identifying images; distorted text) that is easy for humans but difficult for computer programs to solve

question: What is SCREEN TIME and why is it important to manage it?
option_a: The brightness setting of a screen
option_d: The TOTAL TIME spent looking at digital screens (computers; phones; tablets; TV) — managing screen time is important for eye health; physical activity; sleep quality; and maintaining real-world relationships

question: What is DIGITAL FOOTPRINT?
option_c: The TRAIL OF DATA left by a person's online activities — including website visits; posts; comments; likes; form submissions; and purchases — that can be tracked; stored; and retrieved

question: In Book 5; students learn RESPONSIBLE USE of the Internet. Which of these is an example of responsible use?
option_a: Using trusted websites; citing sources; avoiding suspicious links; and telling an adult when something online seems wrong
option_c: Copying all text from a website directly into a school project without citing the source
option_d: Opening email attachments from unknown senders

question: What does the HISTORY feature in a web browser show?
option_b: A CHRONOLOGICAL LIST of all websites visited in the current and recent browsing sessions — accessible via Ctrl+H in Edge and Chrome

question: What keyboard shortcut opens BROWSER SETTINGS / HISTORY / DOWNLOADS in Edge?
option_c: Ctrl+Shift+Delete opens Clear browsing data; Ctrl+H opens History; Ctrl+J opens Downloads in Edge and Chrome

question: What is a BROWSER EXTENSION (or ADD-ON)?
option_d: A SMALL SOFTWARE PROGRAM that adds extra features or functionality to a web browser — examples: ad blockers; password managers; grammar checkers; screenshot tools

question: What is an AD BLOCKER browser extension?
option_a: A browser extension that PREVENTS ADVERTISEMENTS from loading on web pages — improving page load speed; reducing data usage; and removing distracting or intrusive ads
option_b: A tool that blocks all websites

question: What is the difference between a VIRUS and a WORM in computing?
option_b: A worm is less harmful than a virus
option_c: A VIRUS attaches to files and requires a USER ACTION to spread (opening a file); a WORM is SELF-REPLICATING and spreads AUTOMATICALLY across networks without user interaction
option_d: A virus is worse than a worm

question: What is a TROJAN HORSE in computing?
option_b: MALWARE DISGUISED as legitimate or useful software — once installed; it may steal data; create backdoors; or download other malware without the user knowing

question: What does 'UPDATE YOUR SOFTWARE' mean and why is it important for security?
option_a: SOFTWARE UPDATES patch SECURITY VULNERABILITIES — bugs in old software that hackers can exploit. Keeping operating systems; browsers; and antivirus up to date closes known security holes
option_b: Updates change the look of the software

question: What is PEER-TO-PEER (P2P) FILE SHARING and what risks does it carry?
option_d: A method of sharing files DIRECTLY BETWEEN USERS over the Internet WITHOUT a central server — carries risks of downloading malware; sharing copyright-protected content illegally; and exposing your device to strangers

question: What does CTRL+L do in a web browser?
option_c: SELECTS / HIGHLIGHTS the URL in the address bar — so you can immediately type a new address or copy the current one without clicking

question: In Book 5; students are taught internet SEARCH TIPS. Which strategy helps find information on a SPECIFIC WEBSITE?
option_a: Use the 'site:' operator — e.g. 'site:nhs.uk diabetes' searches only the NHS website for information about diabetes
option_b: Put the website name in quotes

question: What is GOOGLE CLASSROOM (or similar LMS) and how does it relate to internet use in schools?
option_b: A LEARNING MANAGEMENT SYSTEM (LMS) — an online platform where teachers post assignments; share resources; collect student work; and communicate — accessed via a browser using school login credentials

question: What is INTERNET ADDICTION and why is it a concern?
option_a: Using the internet for school work
option_d: When a person uses the internet COMPULSIVELY and finds it difficult to LIMIT use; leading to negative effects on health; relationships; schoolwork; and daily life

question: What is AUTOCOMPLETE in a search engine or browser address bar?
option_a: A way to automatically fill in forms
option_c: A feature that SUGGESTS completions based on what you start typing and your search/browsing history — helping you find what you need faster without typing the full URL or query

question: What is a "computer network"?
option_b: Two or more computing devices connected together to share resources, data, and services

question: What is a "PAN" (Personal Area Network)?
option_c: A very short-range network (usually up to 10 metres) connecting personal devices around one person — e.g., phone, smartwatch, earbuds via Bluetooth

question: What is a "LAN" (Local Area Network)?
option_d: A network covering a small geographical area — a home, school, or office building — connecting devices within that space

question: What is a "MAN" (Metropolitan Area Network)?
option_a: A network that spans a city or metropolitan area — larger than a LAN but smaller than a WAN

question: What is a "WAN" (Wide Area Network)?
option_b: A network spanning large geographical areas — countries or continents — connecting multiple LANs; the Internet is the largest WAN

question: What is a "client-server" network model?
option_c: A model where client computers request services and a powerful central server provides those services

question: What is a "peer-to-peer" (P2P) network?
option_b: A network where all devices (peers) have equal status and share resources directly with each other without a dedicated server

question: What is a "server" in a network?
option_a: A high-performance computer that provides services (files, printing, email, web) to client computers on the network

question: What is a "network switch"?
option_d: A networking device that connects multiple devices on a LAN and directs data packets only to the specific device they are addressed to

question: What is a "router" in a network?
option_b: A networking device that connects different networks (e.g., a LAN to the Internet) and directs data packets between them

question: What is a "modem"?
option_a: A device that converts digital computer signals to analogue for transmission over phone/cable lines and back again — connecting a LAN to an ISP

question: What is a "wireless access point" (WAP)?
option_d: A networking device that creates a wireless LAN (Wi-Fi) by connecting wirelessly to devices and wired to the network switch

question: What is the "bus topology"?
option_c: All devices connected to a single central cable (the bus); a break in the cable disables the whole network

question: What is the "star topology"?
option_a: All devices linked in a chain
option_b: Each device connects to a central switch or hub; if one connection fails, only that device is affected

question: What is the "ring topology"?
option_c: Devices connect to a hub only
option_d: Each device is connected to exactly two others, forming a closed loop; data travels in one direction around the ring

question: What is the "mesh topology"?
option_c: Every device connects to every other device; highly redundant — data can take many paths

question: What is a "transmission medium"?
option_a: The physical or wireless channel over which data signals travel between network devices — e.g., copper wire, fibre optic cable, or radio waves

question: What is "fibre optic cable"?
option_a: A copper wire with fibre insulation
option_b: A cable that transmits data as pulses of light through glass or plastic fibres — very high speed, long distance, immune to electrical interference

question: What is "twisted-pair cable" (Ethernet cable)?
option_d: Copper cable with pairs of wires twisted together to reduce interference — the most common LAN cable (Cat5e, Cat6)

question: What is "Wi-Fi"?
option_a: A wireless networking technology that allows devices to connect to a LAN using radio waves (IEEE 802.11 standards)

question: What is a "network protocol"?
option_c: A set of rules governing how data is formatted, addressed, transmitted, and received between devices on a network

question: What does "TCP/IP" stand for?
option_a: Transmission Control Protocol / Internet Protocol — the foundational suite governing how data is packaged and routed on the Internet

question: What is an "IP address"?
option_c: A unique numerical label (e.g., 192.168.1.1) assigned to each device on a network to identify it and enable routing

question: What is "bandwidth" in networking?
option_b: The maximum amount of data that can be transmitted over a network connection per unit of time — measured in Mbps or Gbps
option_d: The number of devices on a network

question: What is "latency" in networking?
option_d: The delay between sending a request and receiving a response — measured in milliseconds (ms)

question: What is a "network interface card" (NIC)?
option_a: Hardware built into or added to a device that enables it to connect to a network (wired or wireless)

question: What is a "MAC address"?
option_b: A unique 48-bit hardware identifier permanently assigned to a network interface card by the manufacturer

question: What does a "firewall" do in a network?
option_c: Monitors and filters incoming and outgoing network traffic based on security rules — blocking unauthorised access

question: What is "network security"?
option_d: Protecting a computer network and its data from unauthorised access, misuse, or disruption through hardware, software, and policies

question: What is "data packet" in networking?
option_d: A small unit of data that a message is broken into for transmission across a network, containing the data and addressing information

question: What is an "ISP" (Internet Service Provider)?
option_a: A company that provides customers with access to the Internet — e.g., broadband or mobile data providers

question: What is a "DHCP server"?
option_c: A server that automatically assigns IP addresses to devices joining the network, eliminating manual configuration

question: What is a "DNS server"?
option_b: A server that translates human-readable domain names (www.google.com) into numerical IP addresses that computers can route to

question: What is the advantage of star topology over bus topology?
option_d: If one device's connection fails in star topology only that device loses connection, while in bus a cable fault disables the whole network

question: What does "Ethernet" refer to?
option_c: A family of wired LAN standards defining how data is transmitted over cables (IEEE 802.3) — the most common wired LAN technology

question: What is the purpose of a "hub" vs a "switch"?
option_b: A hub broadcasts data to all connected ports; a switch sends data only to the specific device it is addressed to
option_d: A switch connects to the internet

question: What is a "VPN" (Virtual Private Network)?
option_a: A secure encrypted connection over a public network (Internet) that allows remote users to access a private network as if they were on-site

question: What is a "proxy server"?
option_d: A server that acts as an intermediary between client devices and the Internet — caching content, filtering requests, and providing anonymity

question: What is "encryption" in the context of network security?
option_c: Converting data into an unreadable format (ciphertext) using a key so only authorised parties with the decryption key can read it

question: What is a "network topology"?
option_a: The arrangement (physical or logical) of how nodes and links are structured in a network — e.g., star, bus, ring, mesh

question: What does "full-duplex" transmission mean?

question: What does "half-duplex" transmission mean?

question: What is "SSID" in wireless networking?

option_b: The IP address of the router

question: What is a "network share" in a client-server network?
option_c: A folder or printer resource made available on a server so authorised users on the network can access it

question: What does "ping" command test in networking?

question: What is "evaluation" in the design process?

question: What is "Statistical Process Control" (SPC)?

question: What is a "user survey" used for in product evaluation?

question: Why is it important to evaluate sustainability in a product evaluation?

question: What is "self-evaluation" in design?

question: What is "peer evaluation" in D&T?

question: What does "evaluating against the specification" require the evaluator to do?

question: What is "comparative evaluation"?

question: What is "aesthetic evaluation"?

question: What is a "product specification test" vs "user trial"?

question: What is "ergonomic evaluation"?

question: What is "safety evaluation"?

question: What does "value for money" mean in product evaluation?

question: Why is it important to record evaluation results clearly?

question: What is "colour matching" evaluation in aesthetic assessment?

question: What is the role of "expert evaluation" in product design?

question: What is "function testing"?

question: What is "durability testing"?

question: What is "100% inspection"?

question: What is an "improvement" in the context of a D&T evaluation?

question: What is "environmental evaluation" of a product?

question: What is meant by "objective evaluation"?

question: What is meant by "subjective evaluation"?

question: What is a "design cycle evaluation" (process evaluation)?

question: What is the most important quality of a good evaluation in D&T?

question: What is a "ferrous metal"?

question: What is an "alloy steel"?

question: What is a "mechanism" in engineering?

question: What is a "bearing" used for in machinery?

question: What is a "pneumatic" system?

question: What are the six key elements of colour described in design?

question: What is a complementary colour scheme?
option_a: Colours next to each other on the colour wheel

question: What is a CAD (Computer-Aided Design) program used for?
option_c: Software that allows designers to create, modify, and visualise precise 2D drawings and 3D models digitally — faster, more accurate, and easier to revise than hand drawing

question: What is desktop publishing (DTP) software used for?
option_a: Only for writing plain text documents
option_b: Combining text, images, and graphic elements to create page layouts for print — magazines, books, brochures, packaging, and posters

question: What is an exploded view drawing?

option_d: A drawing showing damage to a product

question: What is the "rule of thirds" in visual composition?
option_a: Using three colours in a design
option_b: Dividing text into three equal columns
option_c: Having three variations of every design
option_d: A compositional guideline where the frame is divided into a 3×3 grid and key visual elements are placed along the grid lines or at their intersections — creating balanced, dynamic compositions

question: What are dimension lines and extension lines in technical drawings?

question: What does "scale" mean in technical drawing, and how is a scale of 1:2 described?
option_a: Scale means the type of pencil used

question: What is a logo and what properties should an effective logo have?
option_a: A distinctive symbol, mark, or combination of symbol and text that identifies a brand — it should be simple, memorable, scalable, versatile (works in any colour), and appropriate for the target audience
option_b: A lengthy text description of a company
option_d: A detailed illustration of the company's history

question: What is white space (negative space) and why is it important in graphic design?
option_a: Wasted empty space that should always be filled

question: What is an infographic?
option_a: A visual representation combining graphics, data, and brief text to communicate complex information clearly and quickly — using charts, icons, and illustrations
option_d: A detailed table of figures only

question: What is the Golden Ratio (φ ≈ 1.618) and how is it used in design?
option_b: A mathematical proportion (~1:1.618) found throughout nature — designers use it to establish visually harmonious proportions for layouts, logos, and typography
option_c: The ratio of ink to paper in printing
option_d: A type of grid with gold-coloured lines

question: What is a Bezier curve in vector graphics?
option_a: A type of handmade curve stencil
option_c: A mathematically defined smooth curve controlled by anchor points and direction handles — used in vector drawing tools (Adobe Illustrator, Inkscape) to create precise smooth curves

question: What is a flat plan in graphic products?
option_a: A diagrammatic overview of all pages in a multi-page publication (magazine, book, brochure) showing the page sequence, fold positions, and content allocation before design begins
option_b: A plan view of a factory floor

question: What is the purpose of a design brief in Graphic Products coursework?
option_a: A list of materials to buy
option_c: A summary of the manufacturing process
option_d: A written statement that clearly defines the design problem, the target user, the purpose of the outcome, key requirements, and any constraints — forming the starting point for the entire design process

question: What are primary research methods in design?

question: What is a design specification?
option_a: A list of aesthetic preferences only
option_b: A description of the manufacturing process
option_c: A detailed, measurable, and testable list of requirements a design must meet — such as maximum dimensions, materials, colours, printing techniques, cost, sustainability, and target audience
option_d: An opinion on the best-looking design

question: What is colour harmony and what is an analogous colour scheme?
option_a: Colour harmony creates visually pleasing combinations; an analogous scheme uses three or more colours adjacent to each other on the colour wheel, creating a naturally harmonious and cohesive feel
option_b: Using as many colours as possible
option_d: A scheme using only complementary colours

question: What is the purpose of presenting design ideas using "crating" in freehand sketching?
option_a: To add a decorative box around the drawing
option_b: A method of packaging a product

question: What is the difference between a prototype and a final product?
option_b: A prototype is a test version — made to evaluate, test, and refine the design; the final product is the fully resolved, quality-produced version that goes to the customer
option_c: Prototypes are always made from card
option_d: Final products are never changed once made

question: What are the Gestalt principles used in graphic design?
option_a: A set of rules about colour mixing
option_c: A set of typography sizing rules
option_d: A set of psychological principles describing how humans perceive visual elements as organised groups — including proximity, similarity, continuation, closure, and figure-ground

question: What is a hatching line used for in technical drawing?
option_b: Thin diagonal lines (typically at 45°) drawn in the cut plane of a cross-section to indicate the cut material — different hatch patterns denote different materials
option_c: To show the outline of a curved surface

question: What is a title block on a technical drawing?
option_a: A standardised box in the corner of a technical drawing containing: title/name, scale, date, drawn by, checked by, material, drawing number, and company/school name
option_b: The title of the design printed large across the drawing
option_c: A decorative border around the drawing
option_d: A summary of the design brief

question: What is a design iteration?
option_a: A mistake in the design process
option_d: A cycle of designing, evaluating, testing, identifying improvements, and redesigning — repeating this cycle until the design meets all specification requirements

question: What is the difference between landscape and portrait page orientations?
option_a: Landscape is for photos; portrait is for text only
option_b: Landscape is an A4 page; portrait is A3
option_c: Portrait: the page height is greater than its width (taller than wide); landscape: the page width is greater than its height (wider than tall)
option_d: Portrait is used in print; landscape is used only on screens

question: What is a visible outline line in technical drawing, and how does it compare to a hidden detail line?
option_a: They are the same type of line

option_c: Visible outlines are drawn in pencil; hidden lines in pen

question: What is a wireframe in web or UX design?
option_c: A low-fidelity skeletal layout diagram of a web page or app screen — showing content areas, navigation, and functionality without visual design (colour, images, or typography)
option_d: A type of font used in interfaces

question: What is the purpose of a centre line in technical drawing?
option_a: To mark the middle of the paper
option_b: A bold line marking the outline of the object
option_c: A dimension line for diameter measurements only
option_d: A thin chain line used to show the axis of symmetry of a circular or symmetrical feature — indicates the geometric centre of holes, cylinders, and symmetrical parts

question: What is marker rendering and why is it used in design sketching?
option_a: A technique using spirit-based or water-based felt-tip markers to quickly apply broad areas of colour, shade, and highlight to a product sketch — giving a fast, professional, realistic rendered appearance
option_d: A printmaking technique using carved markers

question: What is a system diagram in Graphic Products context?
option_a: A drawing of a mechanical system only
option_b: A simple block diagram showing the flow of a system: inputs → process → output, sometimes with a feedback loop — used to model how a product or process works functionally

question: Why is it important to present design work clearly and professionally in Graphic Products coursework?
option_a: Clear, professional presentation communicates design thinking effectively to the examiner and client — it demonstrates your ability to use graphic communication skills and justifies design decisions
option_b: It is not important — only the final product matters

question: What is die cutting in Graphic Products?
option_b: Cutting with a computer-controlled laser only
option_c: A process using a custom-shaped steel-rule die pressed through sheet material to cut complex, consistent shapes — used for packaging nets, labels, and card products in commercial production
option_d: A hand-cutting technique for thick materials

question: What is laser cutting and what are its advantages in Graphic Products?
option_a: A hand tool that uses a laser pointer
option_b: A technique only for metal cutting
option_c: A printing process using laser printers
option_d: A computer-controlled process using a focused laser beam to cut or engrave sheet materials — advantages: precise, no tool wear, cuts complex shapes, sharp edges, and can engrave surface detail

question: What is screen printing (silk-screen printing)?
option_a: Printing directly from a screen display
option_c: A printing method where ink is forced through a fine mesh screen (stencilled to block non-printing areas) onto the substrate — used for fabric, posters, packaging, and promotional items

question: What is offset lithography (offset printing) and why is it used for high-volume print runs?
option_a: A printing process that uses rubber stamps
option_b: A screen-based printing method for fabrics
option_d: A commercial printing process where the image is transferred from a printing plate to a rubber blanket then to the substrate — producing high-quality, consistent colour over millions of prints

question: What is digital printing and when is it preferred over offset lithography?
option_a: Printing directly from a digital file to the substrate (using inkjet or laser technology) with no plates — preferred for short runs, personalisation, fast turnaround, and variable data printing
option_b: Printing that requires a photographic darkroom
option_c: A higher quality method for all applications
option_d: Printing only in black and white

question: What is flexography and where is it commonly used?
option_b: A rotary printing process using flexible photopolymer relief plates — commonly used for food packaging, labels, newspapers, and other high-speed continuous printing on non-flat substrates
option_c: A hand-printing method using flexible stamps

question: What is gravure (rotogravure) printing and what makes it suited to very long print runs?
option_a: A technique of carving into metal plates for hand printing
option_c: A printing process where ink fills engraved cells on a copper cylinder — the cylinder is expensive to produce but lasts for millions of prints without quality degradation, making it economical only for very high volumes
option_d: A screen printing variant for fine art

question: What is embossing in Graphic Products?
option_a: A method of adding colour to a surface
option_b: A finishing process that creates a raised (embossed) or recessed (debossed) pattern in paper, card, or leather by pressing between a male and female die — adds a tactile, premium quality finish
option_c: A photographic technique for adding depth to images

question: What is foil blocking (hot foil stamping)?
option_a: A finishing process where metallic foil is transferred from a roll onto a substrate by a heated die under pressure — producing shiny gold, silver, holographic, or coloured metallic effects
option_b: Wrapping a product in aluminium foil

question: What is lamination and why is it applied to printed products?
option_b: A cutting process for thick materials
option_c: A method of binding pages together
option_d: A protective coating — a thin layer of plastic film (gloss, matt, or soft-touch) bonded to the surface of a printed piece — to protect it from scratches, moisture, and handling damage, and improve appearance

question: What is UV varnish (spot UV) used for in print finishing?
option_a: Protecting printed work from ultraviolet light damage only
option_b: A clear liquid varnish applied to specific areas of a printed piece, then cured instantly with UV light — creating high-gloss, raised areas that contrast with the uncoated surface for a tactile premium effect
option_c: A full-bleed protective coating applied to all printed materials
option_d: A type of ink used in UV printers

question: What is creasing (scoring) in packaging production?
option_a: A pre-cut compression line pressed into card or paper to create a clean, accurate fold line without cracking the surface — essential for accurate packaging construction
option_b: A defect caused by incorrect folding
option_c: A cutting process for thick boards
option_d: A printing defect to be avoided

question: What is perfect binding?

option_c: Folding pages and stitching through the centrefold
option_d: A bookbinding method where pages are collated, the spine edge is roughened, and a strong flexible glue bonds the pages and cover together — used for paperback books and magazines

question: What is saddle stitching (saddle stapling)?
option_a: A type of embroidery on book covers
option_b: A method of binding with a thread sewn in a saddle stitch pattern
option_c: A bookbinding method where pages (printed as a folded section) are opened at the centre and stapled through the spine fold — used for booklets, brochures, and magazines up to ~64 pages

question: What is 3D printing (additive manufacturing) and how does FDM (Fused Deposition Modelling) work?
option_a: Printing three-dimensional text on a flat surface
option_b: A process that builds physical objects layer by layer from a digital file; FDM works by melting a plastic filament and extruding it layer by layer until the 3D shape is complete
option_d: A form of die cutting for 3D shapes

question: What is vacuum forming and how is it used in Graphic Products?
option_a: A forming technique only for metal
option_d: A process where a thermoplastic sheet is heated until pliable, then drawn over a mould by vacuum suction — used to make blister packaging, trays, and display packaging for products

question: What is a net (development) in packaging design?
option_a: A diagram showing a packaging machine's layout

option_c: A 2D flat pattern — all the faces, flaps, and tabs of a 3D packaging shape unfolded and laid flat — which when cut, scored, and folded assembles into the 3D packaging form
option_d: A diagram of packaging distribution routes

question: What is registration in printing?

option_b: The process of signing a new client into a print shop
option_c: A method of archiving finished prints
option_d: The paper weight specification for print jobs

question: What are CMYK inks and why are they the standard for full-colour printing?
option_a: Red, green, blue, and black inks

question: What is a colour proof used for in the print production process?

option_b: A final printed copy sold to customers

question: What is a bleed in print design?

question: What is a printing plate and how does it work in offset lithography?

option_d: A thin aluminium sheet on which the image is formed — image areas attract oil-based ink and repel water; non-image areas attract water and repel ink — exploiting the immiscibility of oil and water

question: What is a vinyl cutter and how is it used in Graphic Products?

question: What is a plotter and how does it differ from a regular printer?

question: What is model-making in Graphic Products and why is it important in the design process?

question: What is PMS (Pantone Matching System) and why is it used?

question: What does gsm (grams per square metre) measure in paper and board?

option_b: The number of sheets in a ream
option_c: The size of the paper sheet
option_d: The colour intensity of the printed ink

question: What is the ISO A-series paper sizing system?

question: What is a crop mark (trim mark) on a printed document?

question: What is a ganging (gang printing) and why is it used commercially?

option_b: Printing with more than one colour simultaneously

question: What is sublimation printing?

question: What are the safety considerations when using a craft knife (scalpel) in Graphic Products?

question: What is a mock-up in Graphic Products and how does it differ from a final product?

question: What is print on demand (POD)?

question: What does "imposition" mean in print production?

question: What is recycled board and why is it used in sustainable packaging?

question: What is a template in Graphic Products and how is it used in production?

question: What is the purpose of a title block on a working drawing and what information must it contain?

question: What is coated paper and how does it differ from uncoated paper for printing?

question: What is a jig in manufacturing context?

question: What is a quality control check in production?
